facts.fact_text: On 10 December 2010 eight individuals, none of whom are applicants in the present case, submitted notice of a public demonstration to the mayor of Moscow.
The notice indicated that a meeting would be held from 6 p.m. to 7.30 p.m. on Triumfalnaya Square, Moscow.

The notice stated that the proposed demonstration was intended to demand respect for the constitutional right to peaceful demonstration and assembly guaranteed by Article 31 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
On 22 December 2010 the Moscow Government's Department for Liaison with Security Authorities informed the organisers that the event had been approved by the deputy mayor of Moscow.
The authorised meeting began at 6 p.m. on 31 December 2010 at Triumfalnaya Square, as planned.
The applicant claimed that he had arrived at the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square with his daughter.

During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant addressed the participants with a speech in which he criticised the criminal conviction of Mikhail Khodorkovskiy, the former owner of the Yukos oil company.

During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant addressed the participants with a speech in which he criticised the criminal conviction of Platon Lebedev, associate of Mikhail Khodorkovskiy.
During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant condemned the corruption in the State administration.
During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant chanted the slogan "The authorities to resign!".
During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant chanted the slogan "Putin to resign!".
During the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant chanted the slogan "Happy New Year without Putin!".
Shortly after seeing the riot police arrest a participant, the applicant was also arrested and put into a police vehicle.
At 7 p.m. on 31 December 2010 the applicant was taken to the police station of the Tverskoy District Department of the Interior.
The applicant remained in detention at the Tverskoy District Department of the Interior police station until 2 January 2011, pending the determination of the charges against him.
On 2 January 2011 the Justice of the Peace found that the applicant had disobeyed the police orders to stop chanting anti-government slogans and had resisted lawful arrest.
The applicant was found guilty of having disobeyed a lawful order of the police, in breach of Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The applicant was sentenced to fifteen days' administrative detention.

At 7.10 p.m. on 31 December 2010, the on-duty police officer at the Tverskoy District Department of the Interior drew up a report on the applicant's administrative arrest under Article 27.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences, stating that the applicant had been arrested in order to draw up the administrative material.

At 7.30 p.m. on 31 December 2010, the district police inspector drew up a report on the administrative offence stating that the applicant had disobeyed a lawful order of the police in breach of Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Tverskoy District Court's appeal decision held that the applicant's detention during less than 48 hours was not in breach of Article 27.5 § 2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of their official duties related to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the performance by them of their official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between five hundred and one thousand roubles or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

Article 27.2 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that the escorting or transfer by force of an individual for the purpose of drawing up an administrative offence report, if this cannot be done at the place where the offence was discovered and if the drawing up of a report is mandatory, shall be carried out by the police.

Article 27.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that administrative detention or short-term restriction of an individual's liberty may be applied in exceptional cases if this is necessary for the prompt and proper examination of the alleged administrative offence or to secure the enforcement of any penalty imposed by a judgment concerning an administrative offence.

Article 27.5 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that the duration of administrative detention shall not exceed three hours, except in the cases set out in paragraphs 2 and 3 of that Article.

Article 27.5 § 3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that persons subject to administrative proceedings concerning offences punishable, among other administrative sanctions, by administrative detention may be subject to administrative detention for up to 48 hours.

Both Sergeant X and Private Y produced identical duty reports stating that on 31 December 2010 at 18.30 Boris Yefimovich Nemtsov was apprehended because he had disobeyed a lawful order of the police in connection with Sergeant X and Private Y performing their duty of maintaining public order and safeguarding the public.

The duty reports of Sergeant X and Private Y stated that the applicant deliberately refused to comply with the lawful orders to cease his actions breaching public order and continued them ostentatiously.
The duty reports of Sergeant X and Private Y stated that the applicant was invited to enter a police van to prevent him from organising an unauthorised meeting at Triumfalnaya Square.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 30 December 2001 provides that failure to obey a lawful order or demand of a police officer in connection with the performance of their official duties related to maintaining public order and security, or impeding the performance by them of their official duties, shall be punishable by a fine of between five hundred and one thousand roubles or by administrative detention of up to fifteen days.
At the end of the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant, accompanied by his daughter, headed across Triumfalnaya Square towards Tverskaya Street.
At the exit from Triumfalnaya Square, the applicant saw the riot police arresting one of the participants in the demonstration.
The applicant claimed that he was arrested without any warning or explanation.
The applicant claimed that he had not disobeyed or resisted the police and had followed their instructions to pass through.

According to the Government, at the end of the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square on 31 December 2010, the applicant had headed towards Tverskaya Street and had begun calling passers-by to take part in another, unauthorised, meeting while shouting out anti-government slogans.
The Government alleged that two police officers, Sergeant X and Private Y, had warned the applicant and ordered him to stop agitating the crowd and to return to the authorised meeting.
The Government contended that the applicant had ignored the warning from Sergeant X and Private Y and had continued shouting out slogans and disobeying the police.
The Government contended that Sergeant X and Private Y arrested the applicant after he ignored their warning and continued shouting slogans and disobeying the police.
The Justice of the Peace dismissed the applicant's request to admit the video recordings on the grounds that the provenance of the recordings was not supported by evidence.

The Justice of the Peace refused to order that the video recording made by the police be admitted as evidence, stating that the applicant's request was not specific enough and that the applicant had failed to prove the existence of any such recordings.

The thirteen witnesses testified that they had heard the applicant addressing the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square and that after his speech he had said farewell and left; he had not made any calls to go on to another meeting.
Six of the thirteen witnesses testified that they had left the meeting at the same time as the applicant and had witnessed his arrest.

Six witnesses testified that the exit from the meeting at Triumfalnaya Square had been blocked by the riot police and the crowd had begun to build up because those who wanted to leave could not do so.
Six witnesses testified that when the applicant arrived at the cordon the police surrounded him so as to separate him from others wanting to leave the meeting, and arrested him.
Eight witnesses stated that the applicant had not been shouting any slogans and had not been acting against the police orders before being surrounded and arrested.
Sergeant X and Private Y testified that the applicant had disobeyed the order to proceed to the police van and had been arrested; he had put up resistance while being arrested.

The Justice of the Peace dismissed the testimonies of seven eyewitnesses on the grounds that they had contradicted the policemen's testimonies and because those witnesses had been acquainted with the applicant, had taken part in the same demonstration and therefore must have been biased towards the applicant.
The applicant was sentenced to fifteen days' administrative detention.
Photographer T. testified that the applicant had not put up any resistance to the officers arresting him.
Photographer T. testified that the applicant had not shouted any slogans or insults and had repeated "Easy, easy" to the policemen while being escorted to the van.
The Tverskoy District Court decided not to take cognisance of photographer T.'s testimonies, his recording or the photograph submitted at the appeal hearing.

The Tverskoy District Court concluded that the submitted footage did not show the applicant's actions immediately before his placement in the police van and did not depict the applicant addressing the citizens before he was detained, and therefore did not refute the testimonies of Sergeant X and Private Y.
The Tverskoy District Court found, on the basis of the testimonies and reports of Sergeant X and Private Y, that the applicant had indeed been guilty of having disobeyed a lawful order of the police.
The Tverskoy District Court found no reason to mistrust the testimonies of Sergeant X and Private Y because they had had no personal interest in the outcome of the applicant's case.
